gut microbiota is important for host health and disease.
the gut microbial community has an extensive metabolic capacity that is complementary to host metabolism.

the gut microbiome is a complex community of bacteria that is essential for the host's metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, plant poly phenols, bile acids and vitamins, and that the gut microbiotia is an important target for the development of novel therapeutics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying microbial pathways that may have a role in human health, and developing new methods to investigate these processes.
identifying the microbial functions that contribute to host health and disease, and with understanding how they are controlled by the environment and the host
the role of the human gut microbiota in host metabolism, with a particular focus on the metabolic fate of dietary components, and how this may impact human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic potential of gut microorganisms, in particular the bacteria, is enormous and is likely to be much greater than that of the host.
the gut microbial metabolism is a very complex and multifaceted system, which is not yet fully understood.
the gut microbiome is an important contributor in shaping the biochemical composition of the human diet and, as such, it plays a critical role in host metabolism and health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiome has an extensive metabolic activity that is distinct from the host, and is essential for host metabolism and health.
gut microbiota functions: digestion, metabolism of nutrients and non-nutrients, and production of beneficial metabolites.
gut microbial functions are essential for the metabolism of nutrients and food components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiome is an important factor that shapes the nutritional profile of the human diet and, as such, is a key player in human metabolism and nutrition.
the human gut microbiota is an integral component of host metabolism that can influence the bioavailability and fate of dietary and endogenous substances and, thereby, their impact on health.
there is a need to develop more robust and reproducible methodologies to explore gut microbiota metabolism in humans and to identify the specific microbial species involved.
